articles.title: Briefly
articles.content: "Dracula" follows the story of Count Dracula's attempt to move from Transylvania to England in search of new blood and to spread the undead curse. The narrative is told through a series of letters, diary entries, and newspaper articles, focusing on the efforts of a group of people, including Jonathan Harker, Mina Murray, and Professor Van Helsing, to stop Dracula and save Mina from his grasp.

content.title: Good vs. Evil
content.content: The struggle between the forces of good and evil is central to the narrative, with Dracula representing evil and the protagonists embodying the fight for righteousness.

content.title: Fear of the Unknown
content.content: The novel explores the fear of the unknown, particularly in relation to foreignness and the supernatural, reflecting Victorian anxieties about immigration and cultural change.

content.title: Sexuality and Repression
content.content: Dracula examines themes of sexuality, desire, and repression, particularly in the context of Victorian societal norms and the fear of female sexuality.

content.title: The Role of Science and Technology
content.content: The use of modern technology and science in the fight against Dracula highlights the tension between rationality and superstition in the Victorian era.
